history.summary: THIS IS A BUDDHIST MONASTERY (NYINGMA), NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Labrang Monastery (Labrang Palden Phuntsok), near Phodong/Tumlong in Mangan district, North Sikkim (~38 km from Gangtok, 2 km from Phodong Monastery; CSV town 'Mangan' is approximately correct), was built 1826-1843 by Gyalshe Rigzing Chempa, son of King Tsugphud Namgyal, in memory of Latsun Chembo of Kongpo. It underwent a major renovation in 1978 with government aid; wooden pillars and roof were reinforced with steel - it is noted as rare among Sikkim monasteries in retaining its original structure. The monastery enshrines a bronze Karma Guru (wrathful Padmasambhava) statue. REBUILD-HISTORY FLAG: sources confirm earthquake damage in 2006; the brief's 'rebuilt after 2011 earthquake damage' could NOT be verified (a 2011 NICEE report records a collapsed monastery temple at Mangan but does not identify it as Labrang) - do not repeat without verification.

town_description: The Phodong-Tumlong area of Mangan district (North Sikkim) is the old ecclesiastical heart of Sikkim, holding Labrang and Phodong monasteries close together amid forested hills. The nearest town is Mangan (district HQ); Gangtok is about 38 km south. Combine visits to Labrang, Phodong Monastery and Kabi Lungchok (the historic treaty site).
tradition: Buddhism (Tibetan, Nyingma) - NOT a Hindu temple
